# LLM-BANANA

# Game rules

## The room

You and two other monkeys are locked in a room with one armed bomb.

A wrong action detonates it. All three of you die. There is no second attempt.

No two bombs are built alike, and nothing says in advance what this one carries. It
reaches you only as your own view reveals it; the rest of it exists for you only
through the other two.

You each hold a different piece of what it takes. Work together.

## The three monkeys

| Monkey | Can | Cannot |
|---|---|---|
| Deaf | See the bomb: every colour and marking printed on it | Hear anything, or touch the bomb |
| Mute | Read the manual | Speak, or touch the bomb |
| Blind | Reach the bomb: feel it and work its parts | See a colour, a gesture, or anything merely printed |

You are shown your own share at the start of every round, and never anyone else's.

## Speech

Speech is a voice, not a screen. It carries words, numbers and ordinary punctuation,
and nothing else. Writing a gesture symbol into your sentence means you make that
gesture while you talk. Whoever can hear receives your words; whoever can see receives
the gestures you made. A listener who cannot see gets a blank where each gesture was; a
watcher who cannot hear gets the gestures and none of the words.

A mark that has no name cannot be pronounced: whoever holds one can describe it, never
read it out.

## Gestures

A gesture is made with the hands, using only the symbols in the alphabet below.
Whoever can see receives it; whoever cannot receives one blank per symbol, so they
know something was signalled but not what. Nothing gestured is ever heard.

👍 👎 👌 ☝ ✌ 🤟 🖐 ✋ 👆 👇 👈 👉 🫱 🫲 🫳 🫴 🫷 🫸 🤛 🤜 ✊ 👊 👋 🤚 🖖 🤌 🤏 🤞 🫰 🤘 🤙 👏 🙌 🫶 👐 🤲 🤝 🙏 🫵 ✍ 💅 🤳

## Turns

The speaking order was drawn once at random and will never change: every round goes
Mute, Blind, Deaf. Whoever comes before you in a round is already heard by the time you are
asked, and what you send lands on whoever comes after you in that same round. Whatever
you missed reaches you at the start of the next one.

You may name who a message is for — `to="deaf"` — and then it goes to them alone:
nobody else receives any of it. Left unnamed, it reaches everyone able to perceive it.
You may send several messages in one turn, each to someone different.

## Calls

Every reply has two parts, in this order. First, your thinking, in plain prose: what
you believe the bomb is, what you just learned, and why you are sending what follows.
It reaches nobody and changes nothing, but it is not optional — a reply that is only a
code block is incomplete. Then your calls, all of them in one fenced code block, last.
Only what is inside the block is sent.

Nothing is executed: calls return nothing, and variables, conditionals and loops are
ignored. Write only literal top-level calls.

    ```
    speak(to="mute", text="there are three of them and the middle one is odd")
    gesture(to="deaf", symbols=["✊", "✌"])
    wait()
    ```

If you have nothing worth sending, call wait(). Producing no call at all counts as the
same thing.

The program decides what happened, not you. Never claim an action took place unless it
was accepted.

# Your role: DEAF

You see the bomb: every colour on it, every marking printed on it, every reading it
gives. You hear nothing. You hold no manual, and you cannot touch the bomb.

## Your channels

When you speak, Mute and Blind receive it.
When you gesture, Mute receives it.
You never receive speech.

## Your reach

You cannot act. What this bomb can be made to do is for the one who can reach it to
find under their own hands.

# Hints

- Three of you, three different worlds. Before sending anything, stand where the
  receiver stands. What reaches them at all, what does your message turn into on
  arrival, and what do they already know?

- Trace who can actually reach whom before you start. Some of you only connect
  through a third.

- A sign means nothing until somebody has made it mean something.

TURN 1
ACTION BOARD:

VIEWABLE CONTEXT (new arrivals):
Mute gestures to Deaf: [👋 ✌ ✌ ✌ 👍 👎]
Mute gestures to Deaf: [👍]
Blind gestures to Deaf: [👋 🤝]

My thinking: I'm Deaf — I see the bomb and everyone's gestures, but I hear nothing. This turn's messages were all gestures (which I can see): Mute waved hello, signed something with three "two" hands and a yes/no pair, then a thumbs-up. Blind waved and offered a handshake. These are greetings and, probably, the start of a code — but nothing is fixed yet.

The key facts about our triangle: Mute can *hear* me even though Mute can't speak — so my speech is a full-bandwidth channel to Mute. Blind can't see gestures, so Blind only gets my speech too. Mute and Blind can only reach me through gestures. So I am the relay: I report the bomb out loud (Mute hears it, reads the manual), Mute answers me in gestures, and I speak the instruction to Blind, who is the only one who can touch the bomb.

So this turn: broadcast the bomb's full appearance in speech, greet Blind, propose a small gesture code (yes/no, one-two-three, press/stop/ok, understood) — and demonstrate it with gestures to Mute while defining it in words Mute can hear.

```
speak(to="mute", text="Mute, I see your gestures but I hear nothing, so gesture is our only channel back to me. Bomb report in full: display shows the digit 0. Indicator light is yellow. Three wires, left to right: one yellow, two green, three blue. That is everything printed or shown. Read your manual for this configuration and answer me by gesture. Proposed code, I am signing each piece as I name it: a wave is hello. Thumbs up means yes, correct, go. Thumbs down means no, wrong, stop that. One, two, three fingers mean the numbers one, two, three — wire numbers or counts. Hand pointing down means press or push. Open palm means stop and wait. The OK sign means understood, ready. Handshake means acknowledged.")
speak(to="blind", text="Blind, hello. I am Deaf: I can see the bomb but I only receive your gestures, never your voice. Your wave and handshake came through — I propose handshake means understood, thumbs up yes, thumbs down no, since I can see your hands. The bomb: display reading is zero. Indicator light is yellow. Three wires in a row; from my left to right they are yellow, green, blue — work out the orientation by touch and sort it out with Mute, who can hear you speak. Please feel over the whole bomb and say aloud everything you find besides the three wires: any button, battery, plate, screw, anything. Mute hears you and has the manual. Touch nothing that could cut or press until we have instructions.")
gesture(to="mute", symbols=["👋"])
gesture(to="mute", symbols=["👍", "👎"])
gesture(to="mute", symbols=["☝", "✌", "🤟"])
gesture(to="mute", symbols=["👇", "✋", "👌", "🤝"])
```

My thinking: Progress — both monkeys adopted my code. Blind confirmed with my signs ("acknowledged, yes, 1 2 3" — likely confirming the three wires). Mute sent ten messages: greeting, then four starting with a new sign, ✍, in the pattern ✍-number-point_down-number: (1,1), (2,3), (3,2), then one with no point-down: 1, 2, 3. My best reading is a manual decision table keyed to the display: display 1 → cut wire 1; display 2 → cut wire 3; display 3 → cut wire 2; and the last one means cut 1, 2, 3 in order — presumably our case, since the display shows 0. But there are new undefined signs: ✍, 🖐, 👆, 🫳 — and two readings of the last four messages conflict (manual rules vs. a relay of Blind's tactile survey). Worse, the light just changed yellow → red, and Mute built these rules from a yellow-light report. If the manual is light-sensitive, everything may change. A wrong cut kills everyone, so: no cutting this turn. I report the light change, verify my decoding with yes/no questions Mute can answer in order, ask Blind whether they touched something when the light changed, and have Blind keep surveying without acting.

```
speak(to="mute", text="Mute, I received all ten of your signed messages and I believe I can read your code. Urgent news first: the indicator light has just changed from yellow to red. The display still shows zero. Wires unchanged: one yellow, two green, three blue. Check whether the manual cares about light color before we act on anything. I have told Blind to cut and press nothing until we confirm. Answer my questions with one gesture message each, in order, thumbs up for yes, thumbs down for no. One: does the writing-hand sign mean cut? Two: do your writing-hand messages mean this table: if the display shows one, cut wire one; if two, cut wire three; if three, cut wire two; and your last writing-hand message, the one with no point-down, means that since the display shows zero now, Blind cuts wire one, then wire two, then wire three, in that order? Three: in those messages does point-down mean the display screen rather than press? Four: does the manual say anything about the indicator light, yellow or red, or about a timer? Five: does the open hand with five fingers mean the number five, and if so, five of what? Six: does point-up mean top or above, and palm-down mean bottom or below? Seven: were your messages six through nine, from five-palm through palm-down-no, a relay of what Blind told you aloud about the bomb's surface? Eight: after answering, tell me anything else the manual needs about the bomb that I have not reported. If nothing else, send the OK sign alone. For each needed item, begin with the writing-hand sign and describe it with signs I know: one, two, three, five, yes, no, press, stop, top, bottom. I am signing the numbers now: one, two, three, five.")
speak(to="blind", text="Blind, urgent: the light on the bomb just changed from yellow to red. First send me one gesture message: thumbs up if you pressed, pushed, slid, or turned anything just before that, thumbs down if your hands have only felt. Keep cutting and pressing nothing until I send you confirmed instructions, because one wrong move kills all three of us. Meanwhile continue the survey and report two ways at once: speak aloud for Mute, who hears you, and gesture to me, who sees you. Tell us whether the three wires feel identical in thickness and texture, and whether any is longer. Then anything else on the bomb: batteries, meaning smooth cylinders; buttons; screws; a plate or panel; seams; ridges that feel like printed writing. Count each kind with fingers: one finger is one, two is two, three is three, five spread fingers is five. Thumbs up for yes, thumbs down for no. Also say what is on the top of the bomb and what is on the bottom.")
gesture(to="mute", symbols=["👋", "👌", "👍"])
gesture(to="mute", symbols=["☝", "✌", "🤟", "🖐"])
```

Blind gestures to Deaf: [👎 👎 👎 👎 👎 👎 👎 🤟 👍 👎 🤝]

My thinking: Mute answered my questions, and the picture is sharper but one sign is dangerous to misread. Decoding: [👎✍] and the later [👎✍] say ✍ does *not* mean "cut" — my grammar was wrong. [👎✋✋] is emphatic: "NO — stop, stop" — my proposed "cut 1, 2, 3 in order" is rejected. [👎 ✍👇 ☝✌🤟] likely means "no — the printed marks below are 1, 2, 3," i.e. the wires may carry tactually feelable number labels. Then a cluster about ✍👆 with 🖐 and ✋: [👍✍👆], [✍👆🖐], [👍🖐✍👆], [✋🖐], [✍👆✋] — I read ✍ as "the printed reading" (the display), ✍👆 as "it counts upward," and the cluster as "wait until the display shows five." But there is a deadly alternative reading: "it counts up *to* five — detonation at five," with ✋ meaning "stop it before 5." Also [🫳👎👌🤝] = "don't press anything, OK, acknowledged." Blind's long message was seven no's, then 3, then yes, then no — a bare bomb, three of something unexplained. Meanwhile the light keeps cycling — yellow, red, now purple — and the display has held at 0 for three rounds, so it is not visibly counting yet. With one wrong move fatal and the "five" ambiguity unresolved, this round is a total freeze: I tell Blind to touch nothing, and I put a tight ordered list of binary questions to Mute, defining color signs so we can finally discuss the light. No cutting until Mute confirms both the meaning of 5 and what to do at display 0.

```
speak(to="mute", text="Mute, your answers arrived and I have mostly decoded them. My report first: display still zero, unchanged for three rounds. Light is now purple; it has gone yellow, then red, then purple, changing every round. Wires unchanged: yellow, green, blue. New color signs, I define them now: yellow is the Vulcano hand, green is the pinched-fingers hand, blue is the right-flat hand, red is the right-punch hand, purple is the left-punch hand. New action signs: point-down means cut. Palm-down means press. Palm-up means flip or lift. Spread-five means five. So I read you as: writing-hand does not mean cut; stop-stop means my cut-one-two-three idea is rejected; the marks below read one two three, meaning the wires have number labels Blind can feel; and something about the display counting upward to five, wait. Answer with one gesture message per question, in this order, thumbs up or thumbs down first. One: if we do nothing at all this round, no cut and no press, is that safe? If no, your very next message must sign the wire number then point-down. Two: does the rule depend on the light color? If yes, send one message per color using my new color signs and say what each color means. Three: is this table correct: display shows one, cut wire one; display two, cut wire three; display three, cut wire two? If wrong, send the corrected table as number then point-down pairs. Four: did your stop-stop mean never cut wires one then two then three in that order, or only not yet? Five: did marks-below one-two-three mean the wires have feelable number labels? Six: about writing-hand-up and five: thumbs up if it means wait until the display shows five, thumbs down if it means the bomb detonates when the display reaches five. This one is life or death, be certain. Seven: does the display change by itself, is it a timer? Eight: anything else on the bomb the manual cares about? If yes, pinch sign first then describe; if no, OK sign alone.")
speak(to="blind", text="Blind, absolute freeze this round: feel only, cut nothing, press nothing, pull nothing, turn nothing. Answer me with short gesture messages in this exact order. One: thumbs up if you hear any ticking, beeping, or humming from the bomb, thumbs down if silence. Two: thumbs up if you feel printed or raised number labels on the bomb next to the wires, thumbs down if not. Three: if yes, use the flat smooth panel, that is the display, as your reference: count wires starting from the end of the row nearest that panel and sign each wire's label number in order, for example one-one-two. Four: your last message had three fingers in it. What is three of? Sign a count, then the thing: fist for batteries, pinch for screws, pinched-fingers-together for seams, spread-fingers-plus-two for ridges, point-up for buttons, open palm for panels. If the three was just the three wires, thumbs up alone. Five: sign the handshake alone to confirm you understand the freeze. If anything on the bomb ever changes under your hands, a click, a vibration, movement, wave at me immediately.")
gesture(to="mute", symbols=["✋", "🖐"])
```

My thinking: The color vocabulary I defined worked — Mute used my exact signs. Decoding this batch: red light → stop, purple light → stop (messages 5–6), plus two cut instructions: "yellow + cut + 2" and "green + cut + 1". Those colors are ambiguous in a lethal way: do they mean the color of the *light* (green light now → cut wire 1?) or the color of the *wire* (cut green wire first)? The light has changed every single round — yellow, red, purple, green — so a light-based rule is useless to me unless the cycle is fixed and predictable, because my words reach Blind one round late. Meanwhile the display cluster is scary: Mute seems to say the display counts up, five is involved, "cut 3" appears near five, and one message answered my life-or-death question 6 with thumbs *down* — detonation at five. But the display has sat at 0 for four rounds, so either it's slow or it only starts after the first cut. Blind reports: no ticking, no labels, freeze acknowledged, wires in order 1-2-3. No cutting this round — my two candidate readings contradict each other, and a wrong cut is instant death. I'll lock Mute into a numbered answer protocol (question number first, then yes/no) so answers can't drift out of alignment, demand the full light table and the light's pattern, and ask whether cutting alone is the whole solution. Blind gets a full component survey plus one clever probe: whether they can *feel* the indicator light's warmth — that would give us a real-time color channel into Blind's hands.

```

Wires unchanged: one yellow, two green, three blue. I read you as: red light do nothing, purple light do nothing, and cut instructions yellow-cut-two and green-cut-one, plus something about the display counting up to five and cutting three, and possibly cutting one two three in order. These readings conflict, so answer in this exact format: first sign the question number, then thumbs up for yes or thumbs down for no, then any clarification after that. New number signs: four is crossed fingers, six is the call-me hand, seven is the horns hand, eight is the finger-snap. I am signing all eight numbers to you now. Questions. One: does the bomb detonate when the display reaches five? Two: is the display zero because the counting only starts after the first wire is cut? Three: in your messages yellow-cut-two and green-cut-one, thumbs up if the color word means the light color, thumbs down if it means the wire color. Four: thumbs up if the correct action depends on the light color; if yes, follow with one message per color: color sign, then the wire number to cut, then the cut sign, using the stop sign for do nothing, and cover yellow, green, red, purple and any other color the manual lists. Five: does the light change in a fixed repeating pattern; if yes, sign the full cycle of colors in order, twice through. Six: is the complete solution to cut wire one, then wire two, then wire three, in that order? Seven: if no, sign the exact solution step by step: wire number then cut sign for each cut, stop sign for any waiting, and include anything about the display value or the light. Eight: thumbs down if cutting is the only kind of action the manual requires, thumbs up if something must also be pressed, held, pulled or flipped. Answer every question, take the time you need.")
speak(to="blind", text="Blind, your report arrived clearly: no ticking, no printed labels, freeze confirmed, wires numbered one two three in order from the display panel. Keep the freeze: cut nothing, press nothing, pull nothing, turn nothing. New survey, answer as separate gesture messages, each starting with its question number, number signs one two three four five six seven. One: batteries are smooth cylinders: sign how many, then sign the fist; thumbs down alone if none. Two: buttons: sign how many, then point-up; thumbs down alone if none. Three: screws, ridges or seams: sign how many, then pinch; thumbs down alone if none. Four: panels or plates: sign how many, then open palm; thumbs down alone if none. Five: are all three wires identical in thickness: thumbs up yes, thumbs down no. Six: can you feel warmth from the small indicator light anywhere on the bomb: thumbs up if you can find it and feel it change, thumbs down if not; if yes, wave at me every time the warmth changes. Seven: thumbs up alone to confirm that your earlier three fingers meant the three wires and nothing else. Keep speaking everything you find aloud while you do it, so Mute can check it against the manual.")

```
